transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah… I guess what brings me in is my eating has gotten kind of out of hand, especially on late work nights. I’m a graphic designer, so I’ll be up finishing something and I’ll order what I tell myself is just dinner, but then it’s like… a whole entrée, sides, dessert, and then I’m still going into the kitchen for extra snacks.

It feels like way more than I’d ever eat if someone were sitting across from me. I don’t know, it’s embarrassing to say out loud.
After these episodes of eating a large amount, do you ever make yourself vomit or do something else to try to 'undo' the food you ate?

Um… I don’t know, I mean, I get really upset afterward and I’ll think, like, “Why did I do that?” But I’m not sure what counts as “undo.” I don’t think I have, like… a clear thing I do after. Sometimes I just try not to think about it and go clean up the kitchen, or I’ll get distracted by work stuff again because there’s always another email or client note. But as far as what you’re asking… I’m not really sure.
During these episodes when you're eating more than you planned, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control what you're eating?

Yeah… I think that’s exactly it. Like, I’ll start out thinking I’m just going to have what I ordered, and then there’s this point where I’m almost watching myself keep going back—clicking on more food, or opening another package in the kitchen—and I’m thinking, “Okay, stop, you’ve had enough.”

But it doesn’t really feel like a normal decision anymore. It’s like it’s already gotten away from me. I don’t know if that makes sense. It reminds me of when I’m deep in a design project and I keep tweaking something past the point where it’s helpful, except with food it feels worse, because I know I should stop and I just… don’t.
Do these episodes of eating more than you plan usually leave you feeling distressed or affect your work or personal life?

I mean… distressed, yeah, I think so, but it’s hard for me to separate it out. Like, work is already stressful because clients will say something like “make it pop” and then I’m trying to decode what that even means at 11 p.m., and then suddenly I’m eating, and afterward I feel awful and kind of foggy.

As far as affecting my life… I don’t know. I haven’t really tracked it like that. I mostly just try to move on and pretend it didn’t happen. It’s embarrassing, so I don’t usually tell people.

The lack of regular compensatory behaviors (e.g., vomiting, laxative use) and the less clear impact on personal/work life may rule out F50.0 (Anorexia nervosa) to some extent, but it remains a candidate given possible atypical presentation. F50.9 (Eating disorder, unspecified) is ruled out due to sufficient detail supporting a more specific diagnosis.
